correctness.rationale: Direct interval geometry gives exactly four disjointness orientations and the fifth-power sum yields the exact polynomial. Equality of nonzero products forces one of a=u,c=a,w=u,c=w, hence at most 4n^5 possibilities. After dividing by the square of 1+sum_{j=1}^n j^2, the limiting 3/10 and zero-product dominance follow. Independent finite direct-composition checks n=1..10 verify the polynomial but are not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: Commuting probability is an intrinsic structural invariant of a natural inverse monoid. The 3/10 nonzero constant, exact zero-zero count, and asymptotic dominance of annihilation reveal that most observed commutation comes from vanishing products rather than nonzero commuting maps; not merely a reparametrization or an unmotivated finite slice.
